title: Do you need a common denominator?
text: Multiplication does not need a common denominator. Multiply straight across, then simplify. You can also cancel a common factor before you multiply, which keeps the numbers smaller. A common mistake is to add the denominators as if this were an addition problem. After canceling a factor of 2 from 2 and 8, what numerator is left from the first fraction?

title: Cancel a factor of 3 as well
text: 3 and 9 share a factor of 3. Canceling it leaves 1 in the first denominator and 3 in the second numerator. The product is then $$\frac{1}{1} \times \frac{3}{4}$$. What is that product, as a fraction in lowest terms? Use the value of $$\frac{3}{4}$$.

title: Worked solution
text: $$\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{9}{8} = \frac{2 \times 9}{3 \times 8} = \frac{18}{24} = \frac{3}{4}$$. Canceling first: $$\frac{1}{1} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$$. Common mistake: adding denominators, or forgetting to simplify $$\frac{18}{24}$$. General rule: to multiply fractions, multiply numerators and multiply denominators, then simplify. Canceling a common factor before multiplying is the same operation, done earlier.
